newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's June rubber output up 15.5 pct mth/mth.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's June rubber output up 15.5 pct mth/mth.

text.p: Malaysia's rubber production rose 15.5 percent to 82,856 tonnes in June this year from 71,734 in May, the national Bernama news agency reported.
However, the output was 1.3 percent or 1,088 tonnes lower compared to the 83,944 tonnes produced in June 1995, Bernama said late on Friday, quoting data provided by the Statistics Department.
Rubber exports for June totalled 75,170 tonnes, an increase of 6.2 percent from May this year and a drop of 2.4 percent from June 1995.

United States was the largest buyer of Malaysian rubber for the first six months of the year, consuming 12.6 percent of the total exported. South Korea was the second biggest consumer with 11.3 percent and Germany third with 8.0 percent.
Imports of rubber for threading and making gloves, tyres and tubes was mainly from Thailand, followed by the Philippines, Liberia, Burma, Vietnam, Ivory Coast and Cambodia.
Imports in June totalled 24,186 tonnes, up 11.6 percent from May and 9.1 percent higher than June last year.
Local consumption of rubber in June totalled 30,507 tonnes, up 2.8 percent from May and 16.1 percent higher than June 1995.
